title: Risk of Osteoporosis in patients with psoriatic arthritis
summary:
In this study we aim to analyse bone health in patient with psoriatic arthritis. Psoriatic arthritis is a chronic rheumatic disease that leads to inflammation of the joints and is generally associated with the skin disease psoriasis. 
Other rheumatic diseases are already shown to decrease bone health and increase the risk of osteoporosis. Osteoporosis is characterized by a reduction of bone mass that can increase the risk of non-traumatic fractures.
To investigated bone health of patients with psoriasis arthritis, clinical data such as commodities, other risk factor for osteoporosis and medication will be analysed. 
The analysis will be based on routinely collected clinical data and no data will be collected specifically for this study.
Identifying information will be excluded from the analysis.

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of patients diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis who underwent a bone mineral density assessment between 2021 and 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who received treatment between 01.06.2021 and 31.05.2026 at the University Hospital Cologne.
Exclusion criteria:
Only data sets with DXA measurements at the lumbar spine and femoral neck will included. All other locations of measurements will not be considered in this study.
